# Nightgate

> Your coding agents work all night. In the morning, Nightgate shows you only the decisions that are yours, judged by Muse Glimmer on your own hardware.

Every overnight agent writes the same JSON report card when it stops. A narrow rule floor catches git push, production deploys, migrations, and payments with no model call. Muse Glimmer judges every other ask against six kinds of human decision: hard to undo, goes outside, database, product direction, customers, and account or money. Anything unsure ends with the human. Claims like "tests pass" are re-checked. The human's "this needed me" or "the agent could have decided" clicks become training data for a LoRA on Glimmer.

Status: v0.1.0. The Meta Model API tier has not been called, the LoRA has not been trained, and the evaluation set from real nights is not labelled yet.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/woorichicken/nightgate#readme): how it works, Glimmer setup, environment variables, measurements
- [Report card format](https://github.com/woorichicken/nightgate/blob/main/prompts/agent-card.md): the instructions to append to an overnight agent's prompt
- [Training data policy](https://github.com/woorichicken/nightgate/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-training-data-policy.md): which decisions may train the judge
- [Docs page](https://nightgate.solhun.com/docs)
- [Changelog](https://nightgate.solhun.com/changelog)
- [Roadmap](https://nightgate.solhun.com/roadmap)

## Install

Needs Node 22.18+. TypeScript runs directly, with no build step.

- `git clone https://github.com/woorichicken/nightgate && cd nightgate && pnpm install`
- `node src/cli.ts seed` copies the example cards in
- `node src/cli.ts review` judges them
- `node src/cli.ts serve` opens the console on http://127.0.0.1:4777
